name: Marta Quillfeather

loved: {item}! Oh, you dear thing. This will go in my best tonic.
Perfect! The garden thanks you, and so do I.
liked: {item}. Lovely. I know exactly what to do with this.
neutral: Ah, a gift! You spoil me.
disliked: Hm. I'll find a use for it. Eventually.
Not my favourite, dear, but thanks.
hated: {item}?! Child, do you want me to faint?

arrival: Oh, my dear. At last, a place with a proper still and a pot garden.
I'm Marta. Herbalist, healer, grower of very stubborn things. I've been wandering to find a place that would let me plant roots, quite literally.

arrival.say: I'm old, but my potions are young. May I settle here?

choices.text: Please. We'd be lucky to have you.
reply: Aren't you sweet. I'll bring my seedlings.

choices.text: Do you make anything for sore feet?
reply: Ha! Sit down, dear. I'll fix that and more.

arrival: Come by the shop anytime. I'll have the kettle on.
bouquet_reject: Oh my! Flowers. I'm flattered, but I'm old enough to be your grandmother. Keep them for someone your age, dear.

greetings.say: My birthday! Ha, I've lost count of the candles. Come, have some honey cake.
Mind the jars, dear. Some of them bite.
Look at you. Rosy cheeks. Whatever you're doing, keep doing it.
Rain's wonderful for the garden. Sit, drink some tea.
Morning! The dew is perfect for picking. Come help?
Evenings are for the garden. It sings to those who listen.
{player}, my dear. You're the grandchild I never had.

script: Ah, {player}! Just in time for a pop quiz.
*She holds up three sprigs: lavender, mint, and something suspiciously fuzzy.*

script.say: Which of these is good for a sore throat?

reply: Close! Mint cools. But lavender soothes. Remember that for next time.
Brilliant! A natural. You'll be brewing in no time.
NO! That's sneezewort! Don't ever eat the fuzzy one.

script: *Marta stands at the shop door, drenched, holding a satchel.*
A traveller down the road is burning with fever. I need white clover, ginger root, and a steady hand.

script.say: My knees won't carry me through the mud tonight. Would you fetch the herbs?

choices.text: Of course. Where do I find them?
reply: She tells you: the clover grows by the old well, the ginger by the stream.
*Later, the fever breaks. Marta presses your hands.*
*You hold her arm through the mud. The traveller recovers by morning.*
Strong arm, kind heart. A rare pair.

script: *Marta kneels in her garden, her fingers black with soil.*
Come here, {player}. I want to tell you about my garden.
Every plant here is descended from a seed my own teacher gave me. She carried them across mountains.

script.say: I'm not getting younger. When I'm gone, someone must keep these seeds alive. Would you promise to?

reply: *She presses a small pouch into your hand.*
Plant them in good soil, dear. And whisper to them.

choices.text: You'll be here for years yet.
reply: Ha! Flatterer. Yes. Probably. But promise anyway.

choices.text: I'm not much of a gardener.
reply: Everyone starts with dirt under their nails. Think about it.

script: {player}, you've been a good friend. Time you learned the secret.
The recipe for a long life isn't in the jars. It's laughter, honey, and never letting a good friend eat alone.

script.say: Eighty-three years, and that's all I've learned. Promise me you'll remember it?

reply: Take this. A little something for the road ahead.

choices.text: I'll make it my own recipe.
reply: That's the spirit. Every recipe's a little different.
